position-mm.label: DESIGN TARGET
position-mm.why: word/anchor position error vs a reference (REF-W max/p95, REF-R worst anchor, DANFE-L1, LET-1). 0.1 mm (0.28 pt, 0.38 CSS px) is 10x the 0.01 mm the values are reported with and below one CSS px (0.26 mm), the smallest step a px-snapping layout can move; the measurement is deterministic for one build and one reference (CONFIRMED: equal inputs gave equal values in the Phase A repeat run).

geometry-excess-mm.label: DESIGN TARGET
geometry-excess-mm.why: distance OUTSIDE a specification window (BOL-G*, DANFE-B*, DANFE-M1, TXT-A1). Inside the window the spec admits any value, so only the excess is ratcheted; 0.05 mm is about one 600 dpi raster pixel (0.042 mm), the measurement quantum of measure_bars.py / the page ink box.

font-excess-pt.label: SPEC-derived tolerance unit
font-excess-pt.why: font-size excess outside a window; 0.05 pt is the tolerance ACCEPTANCE.md already applies to every font-size criterion (BOL-T*, DANFE-F*).

count.label: DESIGN TARGET
count.why: integer counts from deterministic tools (required strings found, extractor missing/extra tokens, segments/glyphs attributed, decoded symbols): any loss is a real change of the document.

page-delta.label: DESIGN TARGET
page-delta.why: |vellora pages - reference pages|: a page break moving is never noise.

pdf-probe-pt.label: DESIGN TARGET
pdf-probe-pt.why: per-word |dx| / |dy| of vellora's PDF vs Chrome's PDF (pdf-probe semantics 2: PyMuPDF pen origin and baseline, same-page position pairs keyed by the Chrome word). 1 pt (0.35 mm) is an order of magnitude below the Phase A regressions it must catch (invoice price column +9 pt, notification signature -14 pt) and above the 0.01 pt rounding of the probe and sub-px snapping differences. The per-fixture unpaired-word counts use the count class.

acceptedAs.reason: pass -> fail vs the pin (shipped main). The OLD pass was false: the published engine drops a U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE that starts a line, whatever `hanging-punctuation` says (U+3000 is not collapsible white space, CSS Text 3 §4.1), so the down arrow sat at the reference's x without anything hanging; removing the property from the test does not change the pin's render. Neither engine supports the property: `hanging-punctuation` is absent from Stylo 0.18.0 (the pin's) and 0.22.0 (beta.4's), so the declaration is dropped in both. A 1 em ideographic space that does not hang is what the spec gives without the property, and Chrome 155 (which does not implement hanging-punctuation) renders exactly that and fails the test too. The tip lays out U+3000 with its 40 px advance and the arrow 40 px to the right, like Chrome. Accepted as class a by orchestrator decision (a), 2026-10-28; the pin behaviour was UNVERIFIED by the step-4 verifier and is CONFIRMED by Phase C step 05 (evidence 5, 6).
